When I first got on Voat, I thought it was really cool. I loved how you could see the total upvotes/downvotes. It seemed like a rebirth of Reddit before it got so caught up in bureaucracy and money. I was ready for a new beginning. However, Voat seems to be trying to change too much for my taste.

The thing I really dislike about Voat is the heavily regulated karma (not sure of what its called here). Karma is like some kind of rare currency around here. You can't just upvote every post and comment you like, you have to choose out of the "best" ones since you are limited on upvotes. I was certainly no Unidan on reddit, but I did enjoy my average posts getting maybe a handful of upvotes or downvotes. Now it seems only the most clever and witty replies get any attention. I also hate the threshold before you are able to downvote. Having to get 100 points before being able to downvote is a direct cause of the large amount of blatant karma whoring seen all over Voat.

It seems the most active users here have much more influence than your casual user, which is just asking for circlejerks and vote brigading. I liked on reddit how someone who just joined was able to voice their opinion equally to a "reddit celebrity". Reddit was a lot more friendly to casual users.

Does anyone want to explain to me why this heavily regulated karma is a good idea? I get that it's to encourage participation, but come on, lurkers should have the ability to upvote and downvote as much as they please, participation shouldn't be forced. Is this karma regulation planned to be permanent or is it just temporary to try to get Voat off the ground?

I do disagree with Reddit's stance on censorship, but so far Reddit was more enjoyable than Voat has been. I can see myself switching back over in the near future. This being said, I'll continue to use Voat at least through the blackout and even if I switch back, ill check back every now and again to see if Voat has improved.
I'm probably gonna go back to Reddit.
